messages:
alex: Quick sync — thinking about consolidating our SLO telemetry sampling endpoints. Right now we have multiple paths and it makes console queries and routing policies messy. Would like input on an API contract and a safe rollout plan. TL;DR: one endpoint, per-SLO sampling override, shim for backwards compat, surface effective sampling in console.
sophia: +1. Current is confusing: `/v1/slo/tenant/{id}/samples` vs `/telemetry/slo-samples?tenant=...`. I propose a canonical path: `/api/v1/telemetry/slo-samples?tenant=<id>&window=5m` and move sampling controls into request headers or query params. Example curl:
```
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  "https://api.redwood.ai/api/v1/telemetry/slo-samples?tenant=acme&window=5m&sampling=0.01"
```
That keeps queries simple for the console and for tracing.
kevin: Compatibility note: we should not break existing tenants. Plan: add canonical endpoint and deploy a proxy shim that rewrites the old paths for N releases. Also add a response header `X-SLO-SAMPLING: 0.01` so callers know what rate was applied.
jane: One caveat — if we apply sampling at ingestion we might drop low-rate events that are critical for alerting windows. For threshold-triggered evals we need full fidelity for the lookback window (e.g., last 5m). Suggest per-SLO rule metadata: `sampling.default` and `sampling.override_on_eval=true` so evals temporarily switch to 100% for the window.
maria: Quick cost/back-of-envelope: if we keep current sampling at 1% we store ~200GB/day. If we switch to 5% for 5% of SLOs with override-on-eval we add ~50GB/day. Ops budget seems fine but we should add a quota knob per-tenant (daily telemetry bytes) to avoid surprise bills.
ops-bot: deploy-bot posted: "routing: updated staging gateway routes to send `/api/v1/telemetry/slo-samples` to telemetry-shim v0.3. Rolling deploy started 2244501245."
tim: UX: console should show the "effective sampling" value in the SLO header (small pill) and an affordance to temporarily "force full sampling for next X minutes" when running manual re-evals. Also show historical sampling changes in the SLO timeline so users understand why alerts look different.
alex: Good points. Proposed next steps:
- sophia/kevin: draft the canonical API spec (query + headers + response header) and a compat shim plan (keep old paths for 2 releases).
- jane: design per-SLO sampling metadata and eval override semantics.
- tim: mockups for console UI: effective sampling pill + manual override modal.
- maria: run a cost projection with quota scenarios and recommend default tenant quota.
Target schedule: design docs by Wed (2244501300), staging shim rollout Thurs (canary), public migration in 2 weeks behind feature flag. Any blockers?
sophia: No blockers from infra; will add rate-limit guidance in the spec (default 10r/s per tenant for telemetry queries) and an opt-in sampling header `X-SLO-FORCE-SAMPLE` for debug.
kevin: Also add metrics and telemetry for the migration itself: `telemetry.api.requests`, `telemetry.api.sampling_rate_applied`, and a migration_error counter so we can roll back quickly.
jane: One more: include a conservative default where sampling is applied post-aggregation for aggregated metrics, not pre-aggregation, to preserve alert fidelity for derived metrics.
alex: Awesome — let's coordinate on a single-line API example in the spec and I'll open a small RFC thread. I'll ping each of you for reviews. :thumbsup:
